newsitem.title: FRANCE: French barley harvest heads north, yields down.
newsitem.headline: French barley harvest heads north, yields down.

text.p: Barley harvesting in France's north is making quick progress but reports from the Picardie region suggest the crop suffered from a prolonged spring drought, local crop analysts said on Monday.
In the region's three departments of Somme, Oise and Aisne the barley harvest started around July 7. Despite a few showers, some 60-70 of the winter crop had now been cut.
Initial results showed that despite substantial rain in May and June the barley crop did not fully recover from nearly three month of drought and yields are widely expected to decline, analysts said.
"Barley yields will not be terrific this year," an official from the local ONIC grain office in Amiens said.
The latest estimate for winter barley yields stood at 7.5-7.6 tonnes, down from an average 8.0 tonnes last year, he said.
But an expected 10 percent rise in area should allow the region to harvest a larger barley crop this year.
Dry weather in the spring also boosted barley protein content above 11 percent and this would lead to some of the region's barley being declassified for brewing.
"Tests are showing 10.5 percent in some areas but 12.5 percent in others," he said.
But the official said it was too early to say what percentage of the barley would end up in lower-value animal feed.
Average barley test weights ranged from 64 to 68 kilos, he said.
